justification: The daily extract re-read chapters whose current PDF already had a read waiting in review; it now skips them and prints which

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the daily selection query no longer excludes chapters with a pending batch from the same content hash
falsifiable_check.observed_red: before the change the selection read 8 chapters; dry run on production after it: WOULD READ canterbury_bankstown/chapter-7-6 and sutherland ch2 only, 6 printed as [skip]

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_review_queue.source_content_hash and dcp_chapter_registry.content_hash; 6 of 8 flagged chapters had pending rows from the current hash
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: needs_extraction stays TRUE until commit, so flagged did not mean unread
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: adds one NOT EXISTS condition to the existing selection builder and one print of what it skipped

functions.name: fetch_pending_chapters
functions.input: cursor, optional council filter, all-chapters flag and chapter filter
functions.output: the chapters to read, after printing the ones skipped as already queued
functions.if_none: a chapter with a NULL content hash never matches the queue and is read

break_it.scenario: the council publishes a new edition while an old read is still pending review
break_it.what_happens: the chapter could be skipped and the new edition never read
break_it.how: the match is on content hash, so a new PDF has a new hash and is read

break_it.scenario: the reader is improved and a chapter must be re-read on purpose
break_it.what_happens: the skip would stop the deliberate re-read

break_it.scenario: a chapter is skipped and nobody can see why it was not read
break_it.what_happens: it looks like nothing was flagged
break_it.how: each skipped chapter is printed with the reason

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - the next dcp-extract run prints [skip] lines and reads only unqueued chapters
